reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 describes dislocation slip in a V-containing RHEA without carbon or carbides. E2 only states that RHEAs have inferior plasticity. E3 notes carbides are larger at grain/twin boundaries, contradicting the claim of nanoscale, coherent precipitates. No evidence shows carbon addition, carbide formation, or twinning activation in RHEAs.
premises: Interstitial carbon promotes in situ formation of nanoscale, coherent carbide precipitates in RHEAs
These precipitates impede dislocation motion, increasing strength
These precipitates activate deformation twinning, enhancing ductility
